title: Harriet Dart Reaches Her First WTA Singles Final
summary:
A long wait ended in tears of joy.

British tennis player Harriet Dart said it 'means the world' to reach her first WTA Tour singles final, after beating Chinese wildcard Sun Xinran in three sets at the Guangzhou Open. Dart, the British number five, was playing only her second tour-level singles semi-final. She had previously reached the last four at the 2024 Transylvania Open, and she made her WTA Tour debut in Eastbourne in 2015.

'It's been a really long journey,' Dart said. 'I've wanted it so much, so badly — sometimes too much. To finally be here means the world.' She said she found it tough, called the match a rollercoaster, and admitted she had been battling with herself as nerves and feelings grew. She was proud of the second set and of turning things around quickly.

The match swung back and forth. Dart trailed 3-0 in the first set, fought back to lead 5-4, then lost the opener after more double faults as she served for the set. Sun, the 16-year-old reigning US Open junior champion, took her chance. In the second set, Dart twice broke serve and was broken back at once, then twice served to stay in the match before winning the tie-break 7-1. In the deciding set, with Sun struggling and receiving a medical timeout for treatment on her left leg, Dart won every game.

Now Dart faces fourth seed Lilli Tagger in Sunday's final. Victory would return her to the top 100; she has already climbed 14 places to 101st in the live standings. Tagger, ranked 53rd, won her semi-final 6-2 6-0 in 53 minutes.
why_it_matters: Dart's breakthrough shows how years of persistence can pay off even when progress feels slow. It also lifts her live standing to 101st, close to a return to the top 100.

Beating Sun Xinran in the semi-final therefore gave Dart the breakthrough she had been chasing since her WTA Tour debut.
